one_liner: Java framework (Jakarta REST on Vert.x/Netty) that beats nginx's HTTP/2-over-TLS path on HttpArena but loses every scored HTTP/1.1 profile.
what_it_does: Quarkus is a Java application framework (Jakarta REST, CDI, configuration, extensions) whose quarkus-rest module (RESTEasy Reactive) serves annotated endpoints such as @GET @Path("/baseline11") int baselineGet(@QueryParam("a") int a, ...) on the Vert.x HTTP server, which runs on Netty event loops. It builds to a JVM jar (quarkus-run.jar) or a native executable. It is an application framework, not a configurable web server, so it stands in for nginx only where nginx runs a hand-written C handler module, as in HttpArena.
how_it_is_fast: Quarkus moves framework wiring to build time (README: 'We do more at build time, we start fast'), and endpoints marked @NonBlocking run directly on the Vert.x event-loop threads, one per core, with no hand-off to a worker pool. HTTP/2 comes from Netty's codec with stream multiplexing (the h2 profile sends 100 concurrent streams per connection), and the HotSpot JIT compiles the hot path after warm-up. The benchmark entry also turns off Netty buffer bounds and accessibility checks and Vert.x URI and header validation, metrics and context timings. HttpArena gives no mechanism for the h2 lead; h2o (C) runs the same profile 3.45x faster than Quarkus, so the 1.37x over nginx reflects nginx's HTTP/2 path rather than a Java-over-C advantage (inference from page data).
when_to_use: JVM teams that want the Jakarta REST and CDI programming model with event-loop throughput, and accept a framework rather than a toolkit.

HTTP/2-over-TLS APIs serving many small multiplexed requests: on baseline-h2-256 (GET /baseline2?a=1&b=1, 100 streams per connection) Quarkus served 4,668,449 req/s vs nginx 3,414,750 (1.37x), and 4,425,573 vs 3,320,285 at 1,024 connections (1.33x).
Gzip JSON APIs on the JVM: json-comp-4096 served 301,675 req/s vs Drogon (C++) 127,466 (2.37x), though with gzip level 1 (see gotchas).
Pipelined HTTP/1.1 clients (reference-only profile): 7,858,636 req/s vs nginx 4,037,345 (1.95x) and level with Drogon 7,801,404.
when_not_to_use: As a faster nginx or h2o for plain HTTP/1.1, TLS or static files: baseline-4096 0.55x of nginx and 0.50x of h2o, json-tls-4096 0.45x, static-tls-1024 0.47x, static-h2-256 0.22x of nginx (173,987 vs 802,090 req/s, also below h2o's 363,898).

Short-lived connections: limited-conn-4096 (reconnect every 10 requests) reached 564,503 req/s vs nginx 2,626,297 and h2o 2,651,569 while using 3,256% CPU of the 64 threads available, against 6,200% for nginx and h2o, so connection setup rather than request handling looks like the limit (inferred).

Memory-constrained hosts: 10.0 to 11.5 GiB on every HTTP/2, TLS and pipelined row (6.8 GiB on baseline-4096) vs nginx 3.5 to 3.8 GiB and h2o 69 to 308 MiB; even near idle (latency-10k) it held 789 MiB vs Drogon's 72 MiB. The Dockerfile sets ParallelGC with no -Xmx, so much of this is default heap sizing.

CPU-efficiency or tail-latency budgets: latency-1m at a pinned 1M req/s cost 35.0 us CPU per request with p99 1,046 us vs Drogon 32.1 us and 196 us; the 10 KB TLS echo (8gbit-512) cost 164.3 us per request vs Drogon 58.3 us; at 500K req/s on 8 CPUs it held only 64% of the offered rate (Drogon 75%).
Cleartext HTTP/2 (h2c) or gRPC claims: the benchmark entry disables h2c, and its h2c and grpc rows are stale.

integration.form: module (Maven/Gradle extensions io.quarkus:quarkus-rest and quarkus-rest-jackson under the io.quarkus.platform:quarkus-bom, packaged by quarkus-maven-plugin as a fast-jar or native executable)
integration.dependencies: Vert.x core and Netty (via quarkus-vertx and quarkus-netty), SmallRye Mutiny, Jackson for JSON; Netty native transports (epoll, io_uring, kqueue) are optional and must be added explicitly
integration.min_toolchain: JDK 17 to 25 for Quarkus 3.x (README 'Supported JVM Versions' badge); 4.0.0.Beta1 (2026-10-01) raises the minimum to Java 21; the HttpArena entry builds with maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-25 targeting Java 21
integration.platforms: any JVM platform; Linux containers are the stated focus ('Container First'); native executables via GraalVM/Mandrel; benchmarked on Linux x86-64 (Threadripper PRO 3995WX) in Docker
integration.thread_safety: @NonBlocking endpoint methods run on Vert.x event-loop threads and must not block; resource instances are shared across requests (the entry keeps per-thread JDBC statements in ThreadLocals). Detailed threading rules not documented in the sources read.

gotchas: Native transport is not actually on in the benchmark entry: application.properties sets quarkus.vertx.prefer-native-transport=true, but pom.xml has no io.netty:netty-transport-native-epoll dependency; the Quarkus 3.17.8 Vert.x guide says the platform dependency must be added explicitly, and quarkus-netty 3.17.8 marks netty-transport-native-epoll as optional, so the measured runs almost certainly used Java NIO (inferred; the startup log is not published). This handicaps Quarkus rather than inflating it, but the record's flags line overstates the configuration.

The baseline-h2 win is one constant request (GET /baseline2?a=1&b=1, 100 streams per connection, h2load over loopback); on the wire Quarkus answered in about 27 bytes per response vs about 82 for nginx (bandwidth over req/s, derived from page data), so the two servers do not emit the same headers, and h2o (C) reached 16,106,978 req/s on the same profile.

json-comp runs at quarkus.http.compression-level=1: about 1,580 bytes per response vs about 1,392 for Drogon (derived from page data). HttpArena scores this profile by rps times the squared ratio of the smallest response size to one's own, so the raw 2.37x over Drogon shrinks to about 1.84x once the size penalty is applied (derived).

Stale and mislabelled data in the same results file: the baseline-h2c (2.52x nginx), json-h2c and unary-grpc rows predate the current entry, which passes -Dvertx.disableH2c=true and no longer subscribes to those profiles; meta.json and README say JDK 21 but the image runs Temurin 25; the Quarkus rows (2026-08-21) and nginx rows (2026-08-20) come from separate best-of-3, 5 s runs.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Quarkus over Eclipse Vert.x when you want Jakarta REST, CDI and build-time wiring on the same engine; raw Vert.x posted more on HttpArena's pipelined (11.78M vs 7.86M req/s) and baseline profiles, so the framework layer costs throughput. Against Helidon SE it posted more on baseline-h2-256 (4.67M vs 3.61M, separate runs), and Kestrel is the .NET counterpart with similar pipelined numbers (7.44M).
verified_claims_summary: HttpArena on an AMD Threadripper PRO 3995WX (server pinned to 32 cores / 64 threads, load generator on the same machine over loopback, best of three 5 s runs): Quarkus 3.17.8 with RESTEasy Reactive on Temurin 25 with ParallelGC served 4.67M req/s on HTTP/2 over TLS vs 3.41M for nginx 1.31.4 running a custom C handler module built -O3 -march=native (1.37x), and 7.86M vs 4.04M on the reference-only 16x pipelined profile (1.95x). On the scored HTTP/1.1, TLS and static profiles it ran at 0.21x to 0.55x of nginx.
status_note: Very active (last commit 2026-10-12, 3.40.1 latest on 2026-09-30, 4.0.0.Beta1 on 2026-10-01, main merging Vert.x 5.1.10), Apache-2.0 with 15.9k stars and safe to adopt, but the HttpArena entry pins Quarkus 3.17.8, 23 minor releases behind, and its only valid wins over C are on nginx's HTTP/2 path and the unscored pipelined profile.
